references.text: Moses exhorts Israel to be generous toward the poor and not to shut their hand against a needy brother, but to give willingly – this is the background for Jesus' command to give to anyone who asks.
Proverbs contrasts the wicked person who covets with the righteous person who gives without holding back, reflecting Jesus' call to generosity.
The righteous know the cause of the poor – this principle underlies Jesus' words about giving to those who ask.
Jesus' parallel statement in the Sermon on the Mount: "Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you." This is the closest parallel passage in Matthew.
Paul quotes Jesus' words that it is more blessed to give than to receive, expressing the same principle of generosity found in Luke 6:30.
John writes that whoever has worldly goods and sees a brother in need but closes their heart against him does not have God's love in them – a practical exposition of Jesus' command to give.
The promise that there should be no poor among God's people, serving as motivation for generosity and willingness to give.
Paul quotes Proverbs about giving food and drink to an enemy, reflecting Jesus' teaching to give to everyone – even those who take from you.
Isaiah exhorts us to share bread with the hungry and bring the homeless into our homes – a prophetic model for the radical generosity that Jesus teaches.
